provenance.orgName: York, Yorkshire. Benedictine abbey of Saint Mary the Virgin
provenance.p: On fol. 1r is the ex libris Liber monasterii Beate Marie Ebor' (s. xiv). On the same page is the abbey's press-mark: 'In ff.18'. (Note that this should not be taken to be the press-mark of Hereford OFM, as was assumed in New Paleographical Society, First series, II (London, 1903–12), table 17, n. 6.)

history.provenance: Advertised for sale by Bohn. Sale list of Foreign Theology (1839), p. 14 (1842), no. 35.
Joseph Barrois, with the catalog number '345'.
Purchased in 1849 by Bertram Ashburnham, 4th earl of Ashburnham (1797–1878), with other MSS from the Barrois collection; his catalogue number '271' on the inner front board.

Sotheby's, 10 June 1901, lot 271 to Charles Fairfax Murray (1849–1919). [This information about the 1901 sale -- as reported in MLGB3 (2009-2024) -- contradicts the original Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card. The latter states that lot 271 was sold to Quaritch for £89].
Quickly thence to George Dunn, fol. i verso: 'STB G.D. may 1905'; also bookplate: 'From the library of George Dunn of Woolley Hall near Maidenhead".

Sold at Sotheby's, 11 February 1913, lot 511 to the London bookseller John Leighton (£61). This was the last known provenance according to the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), p. 217. The book was likewise recorded as untraced in the Supplement (1987), p. 140.

The following information was supplied in MLGB3 (2009-2024): Sold to the Italian book dealer Basilio Benedetti, between 1913 and 1916, and finally purchased by the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Roma, in 1916, for 3000 lire. Compare also SDBM_MS_3374.
